title: LLM post-training quantization
description: Studying the quality and efficiency trade-offs of low-precision large language models.
motivation: Large language models demand substantial memory and compute. Lower precision is promising, but its value depends on model quality and the way each workload executes.
need: Compare quantized models with 16-bit baselines across quality, memory, latency, throughput, and GPU energy, rather than judging efficiency from model size alone.
solution: Benchmarked FP4, NF4, and NVFP4 against 16-bit baselines across Mistral, Llama, Qwen, Phi, and Gemma.
Measured model quality, GPU memory, latency, throughput, and GPU energy using Python, PyTorch, CUDA, Triton, and NVML.
Profiled quantized execution paths and repeated probes to examine workload-dependent trade-offs.
resultNote: FP4, NF4, and NVFP4 compared with 16-bit baselines.
limitation: The résumé describes the evaluation scope. Aggregate quality, speed, and energy improvements are not published here; no universal efficiency gain is claimed.

title: Multilingual RAG platform
description: A multilingual chatbot that retrieves document context before generating an answer.
motivation: Useful answers often depend on information contained in a specific document collection. Retrieval can give a language model relevant context before it responds.
need: Support document-grounded question answering through a connected retrieval and generation pipeline, including multilingual queries.
solution: Implemented document chunking and embeddings, with FAISS for retrieving relevant context.
Connected retrieval to LangChain to generate responses grounded in the supplied documents.
Used query classification and prompt engineering to support relevant retrieval and answer generation.
limitation: No retrieval benchmark, supported-language list, or production deployment is documented in this portfolio.

title: VoxCeleb speaker identification
description: Closed-set speaker identification across 605 voices using a custom VGG-style convolutional network.
resultNote: 72,766 spectrogram samples · best checkpoint at epoch 45.
summary: A seven-layer convolutional network learns to identify speakers from pre-extracted spectrograms. The pipeline includes normalization, augmentation, stratified splitting, and checkpoint selection.
methods: Frequency/time masking, Gaussian noise, and circular shifts for training augmentation.
Single-channel 256 × 256 spectrogram inputs and 605 output classes.
Training curves reconstructed from saved epoch logs; weighted validation F1 of 0.8641.
limitation: Validation clips are split at the file level, not grouped by recording session. No unknown-speaker verification, independent test result, or raw-audio preprocessing pipeline is demonstrated. The trained checkpoint is not yet included.
motivation: Speech carries information about the person speaking as well as the words being said. This project investigates how a convolutional model can learn those distinguishing patterns.
need: Identify speakers from spectrograms across a large, fixed set of known identities, with a repeatable training and evaluation workflow.
solution: Frequency/time masking, Gaussian noise, and circular shifts for training augmentation.
Single-channel 256 × 256 spectrogram inputs and 605 output classes.
Training curves reconstructed from saved epoch logs; weighted validation F1 of 0.8641.

title: Molecular toxicity prediction
description: Representing molecules as graphs to predict activity across 12 toxicity assays.
resultNote: 7,823 molecules · 80/20 random training/validation split. ROC-AUC is not an accuracy percentage.
summary: A graph convolutional network learns molecular representations from atom features and bond connectivity, with masked binary cross-entropy to handle missing assay labels.
methods: Three graph convolution layers with 128 hidden channels and global mean pooling.
Adam optimization, learning-rate scheduling, checkpointing, and early stopping.
Visual analysis of assay performance, missing labels, molecular graphs, and learned embeddings.
limitation: No scaffold split or independent test set. The notebook’s new-SMILES inference uses a different feature encoding from training; its example toxicity scores are not validated predictions.
motivation: Molecular structure contains relationships that are difficult to capture with flat feature tables. This project explores learning directly from atoms and bonds.
need: Predict activity across multiple toxicity assays while accounting for missing labels and the connected structure of each molecule.
solution: Three graph convolution layers with 128 hidden channels and global mean pooling.
Adam optimization, learning-rate scheduling, checkpointing, and early stopping.
Visual analysis of assay performance, missing labels, molecular graphs, and learned embeddings.

title: ESG risk analysis dashboard
description: English and Marathi dashboards for exploring village-level ESG survey results.
motivation: Survey responses can be difficult to interpret when risk signals are spread across villages, focus groups, and individual questions.
need: Make environmental, social, and governance results easier to investigate at both summary and question level, in English and Marathi.
solution: Built Power BI dashboards covering village-level survey results, risk indices, and ESG dimension scores.
Added filters by village, focus group, and ESG dimension to support targeted investigation.
Included question-level analysis and response counts to help identify sources of risk.
resultNote: Two language views for village-level ESG analysis.

title: Polymer property prediction
description: A team pipeline for predicting seven polymer properties from repeat-unit SMILES.
resultNote: Team project — The Invincibles. Architecture and methods are described in the repository.
summary: A multi-property approach combining graph representation learning, chemical descriptors, structural invariance, and heterogeneous ensembles to study polymer behavior.
methods: CRU mapping to standardize equivalent repeat-unit representations.
MPNN representations and self-supervised pretraining.
Descriptor and fingerprint features, cross-task learning, stacked models, and attribution.
limitation: The repository overview describes the approach; no verified per-property benchmark is presented here. This is a team project, and individual contributions are not separately quantified in the public README.
motivation: The relationship between polymer structure and material behavior motivates learning representations from repeat-unit chemistry.
need: Predict several material properties from SMILES while addressing equivalent structural representations and combining complementary model signals.
solution: CRU mapping to standardize equivalent repeat-unit representations.
MPNN representations and self-supervised pretraining.
Descriptor and fingerprint features, cross-task learning, stacked models, and attribution.

title: Market anomaly analysis
description: A multivariate look at anomalous behavior across three Indian market indices.
resultNote: Nifty 50, Nifty Midcap 150, and Nifty Smallcap 250. Coauthored with Kartik Soni.
summary: An exploratory research pipeline combining rolling feature Z-scores, Mahalanobis distance, cross-index return divergence, and lead–lag regime analysis.
methods: Daily OHLCV acquisition with the FYERS API.
Return, high–low spread, and realized volatility features.
Trailing 126-observation multivariate baselines and cross-capitalization comparisons.
limitation: The coauthored manuscript is unpublished and has not been peer reviewed. Detector flags are not independently verified financial events. No trading backtest or predictive accuracy is claimed.
motivation: Looking at a single price series can hide relationships between market segments. This study explores unusual behavior across multiple indices and features.
need: Create an interpretable exploratory workflow for comparing returns, volatility, and cross-index divergence without presenting detector flags as verified events.
solution: Daily OHLCV acquisition with the FYERS API.
Return, high–low spread, and realized volatility features.
Trailing 126-observation multivariate baselines and cross-capitalization comparisons.

title: News article classification
description: Comparing three classical machine learning models for news article classification.
resultNote: Linear SVM · 11,225 test articles in the notebook’s saved classification reports.
summary: An end-to-end text classification experiment covering dataset inspection, binary labeling, text cleaning, TF-IDF features, model comparison, and manual prediction examples.
methods: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and a linear support vector machine.
TF-IDF fitted on training text and applied to held-out text.
Accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 reported from saved notebook outputs.
limitation: A random article split does not establish generalization to new publishers or dates. Source overlap and repeated articles may inflate performance. This is dataset-based classification, not independent fact-checking.
motivation: Text classification offers a practical way to study how language features influence model decisions. This project compares classical methods on labeled news articles.
need: Build a reproducible text-processing and model-comparison pipeline, while separating dataset performance from real-world fact-checking.
solution: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and a linear support vector machine.
TF-IDF fitted on training text and applied to held-out text.
Accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 reported from saved notebook outputs.

title: Home energy optimization
description: Learning appliance schedules under simulated electricity tariffs, with an interactive dashboard.
resultNote: One simulated day against an always-on controllable-appliance baseline; not real household savings.
summary: A custom Gymnasium environment and Stable-Baselines3 DQN balance electricity cost, a comfort proxy, peak demand, and appliance switching over a 24-hour day.
methods: Eight ON/OFF combinations for AC, washing machine, and dishwasher.
100,000 training timesteps and hourly time-of-use pricing.
Streamlit dashboard with appliance heatmaps, cost comparisons, and a 24-hour replay.
limitation: The synthetic tariff, simplified always-on baseline, and binary controls limit real-world interpretation. The simulation has no realistic appliance-cycle or temperature dynamics.
motivation: Electricity pricing varies over time, creating a scheduling problem for controllable appliances. This project explores that problem through reinforcement learning.
need: Study the trade-offs between simulated electricity cost, comfort, peak demand, and appliance switching in an interactive environment.
solution: Eight ON/OFF combinations for AC, washing machine, and dishwasher.
100,000 training timesteps and hourly time-of-use pricing.
Streamlit dashboard with appliance heatmaps, cost comparisons, and a 24-hour replay.

Implemented scheduling workflows around the relational model.

title: Underground water leakage detection
description: Connecting flow sensors to a live monitoring dashboard and email alerts.
motivation: Hidden pipelines are difficult to observe directly. Sensor readings can provide a more accessible view of changes in water flow.
need: Bring sensor measurements into a live monitoring interface and notify users when the system detects a potential leak.
solution: Used flow sensors and ESP32 hardware to detect pipeline leakage.
Streamed sensor measurements through MQTT to a live Streamlit dashboard.
Added automated email alerts to the monitoring workflow.
limitation: No field validation, detection accuracy, or measured water savings are documented here.
